summary:
Since 1964 is an interactive educational website that introduces visitors to six landmark space exploration missions: the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Ranger 7–9, Spirit, Curiosity, Voyager 1 and 2, and New Horizons. We developed a responsive, English-language experience that combines concise mission summaries, spacecraft photo galleries, a timeline, and playful activities in one space-themed interface.

The project addresses a common challenge in learning about space: information is often spread across technical sources and can feel difficult to approach. Each mission appears in a clear section with key dates, engineering features, and discoveries, allowing visitors to explore at their own pace. Animated rocket launches, colorful fireworks, glowing stars, constellation patterns, a connect-the-stars activity, and a miniature Solar System create visual interest, while a five-question quiz helps visitors review what they have learned.

By connecting early lunar exploration with robotic missions, the website shows how each journey contributed to our understanding of the Moon, Mars, Pluto, and the outer Solar System. It makes space history more accessible, encourages curiosity about science and engineering, and offers an engaging starting point for classroom or independent learning.
details:
Since 1964 is an interactive website about six space exploration missions: the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Ranger 7–9, Spirit, Curiosity, Voyager 1 and 2, and New Horizons. Visitors can explore mission summaries, photographs, a timeline, constellation activities, and a five-question quiz. Animated rockets, fireworks, glowing stars, and a miniature Solar System make the experience more engaging.

The project makes space history easier to approach by presenting complex missions in concise sections with key dates, engineering details, and discoveries. Its benefits include supporting classroom introductions, independent learning, and curiosity about science and engineering. The intended impact is to help visitors see how exploration has developed from the first lunar missions to robotic journeys across the Solar System.

The website was developed as a single-page project using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. Mission photographs are stored in an IMAGES folder, and the public site is hosted with Netlify. No specialized hardware was required.

The creative approach combines educational content with interactive space-themed elements, so visitors can read, explore, and test their knowledge. The team considered the audience’s familiarity with space science, readability, mobile layouts, visual contrast, page organization, and motion sensitivity. The website also includes a photo references section that links to relevant NASA mission archives and explains when an uploaded image’s original credit could not be verified.
